verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's Computer docs say the product embeds real coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Cline and others) as native chat backends. It supervises their file reads, edits and approvals as tool cards with Allow/Deny buttons, and runs parallel agents on git worktrees, so the editing and supervision parts of repo work are directly documented. Test runs appear only as a scheduled-task example, and repo cloning is never mentioned, so not every part of the story is covered. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the agent cloning repositories, testing documented as part of an interactive agent workflow rather than only as a scheduled prompt, and independent or hands-on corroboration that the coding-agent supervision works in practice.

support.subject: As a developer, the assistant can supervise or embed real coding agents so it does repo work — cloning, editing, testing — not just snippets in chat

citations.quote: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Cline, or Pi run as native chat backends using the CLI login already on your machine.
You see the full history: every file it read, every edit it made, and the pending approval that's blocking it, rendered as tool cards with Allow / Deny buttons.
one worktree per task, one workspace per worktree, one agent per workspace, all supervised from a single browser tab.
any OpenAI-style client can run agent tasks in a real workspace.
Schedule a task that runs the test suite every weekday at 9 and reports failures with the error output.
